title: Chapter 2: Walking the Beaten Path Together 1
content: Twelve days had passed.

By the time I no longer felt nervous calling her Erika, could look at her face directly without hesitation, and our skills in the game called Shinru, played in the carriage, began to match each other.
We crossed the border.
Although there was no checkpoint, a stone pillar stood on a prominent hill.
While it was built along the highway, it was something you could easily miss if you weren't paying attention.

I wondered if this was really okay, but the Faltarl Kingdom, our homeland, and the Orclra Kingdom, to which we were heading, were allied nations. Moreover, the first kings of both countries were siblings, and they still maintained blood ties through marriages, making their relationship one that could be described as, "Why not just stick together already!"
It was the first choice for nobles who had been exiled from their homeland.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/duHhY9D.jpeg
However, only nobles who had committed relatively minor offenses were targeted for such exile due to the close ties between the two nations.

In principle, a noble who plotted to assassinate the Light Priestess would not be accepted, but thanks to the earnest efforts of the Faltarl Kingdom, they somehow managed to negotiate with the Orclra Kingdom.
In reality, it was truly a mystery. Finding a country willing to accept someone who plotted to assassinate the Light Priestess was no easy task.
Without a doubt, the relationship with the Church would worsen, and the more I thought about it, the less reason there was for acceptance.
How much did our country pay to the Church and the Orclra Kingdom this time? It was almost miraculous.
Though it wasn't something I needed to worry about, it would certainly be a challenge moving forward.
Well, it wasn't my concern.
"I finally have the upperF hand!"
Erika declared confidently as she placed her piece on the board.
The Shinru board was set up for playing in the carriage, with pegs driven in for the pieces to pass through.
"Even so, it still looks even to me at this forty-move mark."
"If that's the case, Shin, my victory is assured, wouldn't you say?"
She responded to my remark without missing a beat, clearly confident.
"By the way..."
I said while playing with the pieces in my hand.
"The only attack we've faced was that one time."
"That's true," Erika replied, gazing intently at the board.
Her serious expression while focusing on the game, which she had started as a pastime, was beautiful.
"Have you grown bored of me, or is there another reason? Perhaps it's simply that you've run out of pieces?"
While she spoke, she followed the pieces on the board with her gaze, golden magic flowing along with it. Hmm, I see, that's the strategy. I certainly wouldn't win.
"I'd be glad if that were the case."
I considered the movements of the pieces. Where were the critical points?
Ah, I remembered the moves that had caught me off guard at the Adventurer Guild's tavern several times.
"With that kind of resolve, your opponent wouldn't aim for your life, would they?"
As I said this, I moved a piece toward her critical point. Surely, a human bomb wouldn't come at her with such a lighthearted attitude.
Erika made a surprised expression before puffing out her cheeks and glaring at me.
"Was that conversation a form of off-board strategy?"
What a cute and beautiful creature this was.
"Following the moves with your gaze is a poor strategy."
I shrugged nonchalantly and urged her to make her next move.
Erika shot me a look that seemed to want to complain for a few moments, but ultimately said nothing and returned her focus to the board.
"Speaking of which..."
She murmured, breaking the long silence of contemplation.
During that time, her magic swirled rapidly in response to her thoughts.
"The plan was for me to become an adventurer at the border town, wasn't it?"
"That was the plan."
Yes, Erika was supposed to become an adventurer. This was all part of the farce.

Currently, the Solnzali family could not openly support Erika, who had been stripped of her noble status. While the kingdom wouldn't care if the Solnzali family supported their exiled daughter, there were factions that would.
The Church.
To the Church, she was an unforgivable person who attempted to assassinate the Light Priestess.
I didn't know how it had come to this, but through negotiations between the kingdom and the Church, Erika had been stripped of her noble status and was exiled instead.
From the Church's perspective, if that was merely a formality, they would be greatly dissatisfied.
If things went poorly, various situations could turn upside down, which was something both Erika's father, the Prime Minister, and the kingdom did not wish for.
Thus, Erika needed to become self-sufficient after her exile.
At least on the surface.
"If you have something else you want to do, that's fine too."
The reason for making her an adventurer was simply that it was the easiest profession to take up.

Additionally, while she would belong to the Adventurer Guild, it was a freelance occupation. While it might be impossible to do nothing at all, there was a lot of leeway for both extreme laziness and deception.
"I gave up on the luxury of deciding what I want to be a long time ago."
She placed a piece on the board. I see, so she had decided not to give up.
"If that's the case, then I must have been living quite a luxurious life."
I might need to wrap this up quickly; it could get dangerous.
"My father only told me to do as I please... wait, could it be that he just didn't have any expectations for me?"
I was slightly shocked to find myself questioning my parents' affection as I moved my piece in response.
"Shin, you are an adventurer, right?"
"Well, yeah."
I answered Erika's voice, which felt more like a confirmation than a question, as she fell into another long contemplation.
"Though in the Orclra Kingdom, I would be considered unemployed."
"Is that so?"
"Because of the connections between guilds, it's often misunderstood, but the adventurer guilds in each country are independent organizations."
If they point at me there, my strategy would collapse.

"If they weren't, they wouldn't be able to respond to the circumstances of each country. While there's not much difference between Faltarl and Orclra, if you go to another country, the only commonality is the evaluation criteria for ranks. So if I want to be an adventurer in the Orclra Kingdom, I would have to start from scratch."
I suddenly felt her gaze and looked up from the board to see Erika smiling at me.
Stop it, or I'll die.
"It sounds like it would be fun to become an adventurer from scratch with you."
With that smile, she moved a piece toward my critical point.
Strategy collapse, and by the way, my loss was now certain.
"By the way, isn't it a poor strategy to stare at your own critical point so intently?"
She had a triumphant smile that seemed to say she had me.
Orclra Kingdom, Makikomaru Cro Border Barony, the Double Barrier City of Hekatai.
Three days after crossing the border, we arrived at our destination, Erika's and mine.
As the name suggested, Hekatai was a fortress-like city surrounded by a double barrier.

It was the most important city for national defense in the border barony, but the Faltarl Kingdom and the Orclra Kingdom were friendly nations. In fact, the border barony itself did not even face the border with the Faltarl Kingdom.
The Makikomaru Cro Baron was not protecting the country from humans. However, the Makikomaru Cro Barony was indeed a nation located at the border.
Yes, it was protecting the country from the region known as the Demon Realm.
"I had read about it in books, but seeing it in person is quite something."
Erika said as she looked at the barrier surrounding the central part of the city, with the barrier we had just passed behind us.
A barrier within a barrier was a sight one would not see elsewhere.
And the atmosphere of the city itself was unique.
The proximity of the Demon Realm meant that there were many monsters.
In other words, it was a workplace for adventurers.
Thus, Hekatai was famous as a city for adventurers, equal to its double barrier.
The sight of armed commoners walking around was not something one could see every day.
For a proper noble, it would be an unsettling sight, but unfortunately, I had already stepped outside the bounds of being a proper noble, so it didn't particularly bother me.
There was no other city in the Faltarl Kingdom where so many adventurers gathered.

Part of the reason was that there was no Demon Realm within its territory, but also because the frequency of monster appearances in the Faltarl Kingdom was not that high. Instead, strong monsters tended to appear more easily.
Well, putting that aside.
However, in the Orclra Kingdom, where the Demon Realm existed, things were different.
After all, the Demon Realm produced all kinds of monsters in large numbers.

Due to the Demon Realm, the frequency of monster appearances within the territory was high, and if monsters that emerged from the Demon Realm were left unchecked, the Demon Realm itself would expand. Fortunately, powerful monsters rarely emerged from the depths of the Demon Realm, but in exchange, weak monsters and moderately strong monsters would overflow.
Naturally, the country could not afford to leave such things unchecked, so they dealt with it using knights and other means.
However, they could not focus solely on monsters; the country was busy preparing for invasions from other nations and maintaining public safety.
Thus, it became difficult for the country alone to deal with monsters, leading to the establishment of the Adventurer Guild.
Yes, it is said that the first Adventurer Guild to be established in various countries was in the Orclra Kingdom.
Furthermore, the headquarters is located here in Hekatai.
Thus, we arrived in a city where residents casually walked around with swords, spears, and axes, a place that would likely make a proper noble dizzy.
The residence prepared by the Prime Minister was a cozy little house that looked comfortable.
Though small, it had a garden and a fence.
While it was small by noble standards, it would be considered a decent house by commoner standards.

A city protected by a barrier is a precious safe zone for humanity. Naturally, buildings are constructed to extend upwards to make effective use of the limited land. Just having a single-family home is a luxury.
Looking at the neighboring houses, they were all neat and tidy, suggesting that the area was safe.
Personally, I had no complaints, but I wondered how she felt about it.
After all, she was the daughter of a marquis.

If she were to say, "I can't live in such a shabby house," it would certainly put me in a bit of a bind. It wasn't that she couldn't live in a mansion; even if it wasn't immediately possible, the Prime Minister would arrange it if asked.
However, that would defeat the purpose of the farce.
The Church likely wouldn't naively think that the Prime Minister would provide no assistance to his daughter.
Still, it wouldn't be amusing if she were to live a leisurely and indulgent life after being exiled.
After all, from their perspective, the stripping of Erika's noble status and her exile was a punishment for her.
So, I wanted to avoid any risks that might change the Church's mind.
Now, what if she said she didn't want to live here? As I pondered this while glancing at Erika's face in front of the house's gate, she looked at me and smiled.
"It's a nice house, Shin."
I hadn't anticipated such a reaction.
"I truly felt it for the first time when I saw the house."
What do you mean? I asked with my gaze.
"I am no longer a noble; I am a commoner, free, uncertain of the future, and without a defined path."
Her eyes sparkled with intensity.
Ah... those were the same eyes I had seen many times at the academy.
Back then, I had seen them in profile, but now I was looking at her face-on.
"It feels like a stormy night at sea."
"Are you anxious?"
There was no way that was the case; I was certain of it as I asked.
"No, after all, I have a reliable companion on this journey."
With that, she extended her hand toward me.
"Will you enjoy this voyage with me?"
"Gladly."
I took her hand in mine.
"Hey, could you help me carry the luggage soon?"
Merseja said, seemingly exasperated as he unloaded the bags from the carriage.
Since the house was already furnished with furniture and bedding, all we had to do was move in our belongings.
Cleaning had already been taken care of, so there was truly nothing to do.
The only difficulty was that I had trouble sleeping at night, as I kept recalling the feel of Erika's hand.
Though I had decided on room assignments casually, I was slightly scared by the letter from the Prime Minister that had somehow ended up on my bed.
Early the next morning, Erika and I saw Merseja off as he returned to Faltarl.
"We'll look into the attackers here too, but you two should be careful enough."
Merseja briefly looked at Erika with a face that seemed to want to say something but just shook his head.
"Well, I think as long as you're cautious, you'll be fine."
I understood what he wanted to say.
"Thanks for everything, Merseja. I think we'll be relying on you quite a bit moving forward, so I'll pray for your safety on the way."
"Please give my regards to your father, and let him know I'm doing well."
From the looks of that letter, the Prime Minister likely wouldn't be reassured by mere words.
"Take care, young lady."
Merseja said, bowing his head.
"Well then, let's get going."
After watching the departing carriage, I said.
"That's right."
Without asking where to, Erika agreed.
We had discussed it yesterday, and today we were going to complete our adventurer registration.

Becoming an adventurer is the easiest profession in the world; all you have to do is register with the Adventurer Guild. While some countries may require tests, neither Faltarl nor Orclra has such requirements. You become an adventurer on your own, grow on your own, and the unqualified can just die on their own.
This isn't due to the Adventurer Guild's negligence; it's a matter of agreement with the country.
The Adventurer Guild is prohibited from training adventurers in combat skills, including magic, due to agreements with the country.
All they can do is provide knowledge in the form of books.
Thus, it's common for new adventurers to find someone experienced to mentor them.
They learn how to handle weapons and fight monsters through practical training, which is entirely different from the academy that teaches both magic and combat against humans.
Personally, I found the adventurer's way more suited to me, but that varies from person to person.
The academy taught not only how to fight monsters but also how to fight against humans.
Erika and I made our way through the early morning streets toward the Adventurer Guild.
Walking beside Shin, Erika curiously observed the early morning city.

Since humanity acquired the magic stone lamps, which allowed work to continue after sunset, nobles had been waking up later and later. Early morning was commoner time, which was Erika's understanding as a noble.
While Erika often woke up early for sword training, walking through the city at this hour was a refreshing experience.

She found herself glancing around, but Shin walked with a natural demeanor. Though it had only been a short time since they began to spend time together, this Shin was remarkably un-noble in some aspects.
Until they arrived in Hekatai, they had only spent time in inns, so she hadn't realized it, but walking together made it clear.
He was very accustomed to it.
Not to walking around the city; Erika too would walk around if she had business in town.
However, at those times, it was customary for a family member to accompany her. While she had found it bothersome, she also realized that she had thought of it as the norm.
Shin was accustomed to walking freely by himself, which was quite un-noble.
Her best friend had said that while she didn't mind going out together, it felt a bit constricting, but Shin might have agreed with her words.
But now she understood. Shivering with an indescribable sensation, Erika thought about how liberating it was to walk through the city on her own.
Suddenly, drawn by a smell, Erika stopped in her tracks. She was intrigued by a food stall selling food for adventurers who were already up and about in the early morning.
They were selling something made of meat and root vegetables grilled and stuffed in bread.
The way they sold, bought, and ate it could only be described as crude.
But... somehow, it was quite good. There was a certain vitality that was hard to put into words.
The Adventurer Guild was located on the outskirts of the city, so it was a bit of a distance away, but it was interesting enough to not be a problem.

Since Erika had stopped, Shin, who had also halted, asked with just a glance and gesture if he should go buy some, but Erika shook her head in response. While Shin's gesture was quite nice, there were other things they needed to do right now.
She made a mental note to definitely try it next time, and with a gesture, she signaled Shin to move ahead. Hmm, communicating with gestures was also quite crude but nice.
As Erika walked on, she didn't notice that Shin had a slightly creepy smile on his face.
The Adventurer Guild is usually located closest to the barrier in most towns.

Since one of its main businesses is buying monster materials and magic stones harvested from monsters, a certain amount of space is needed for storage. Additionally, it was more convenient to accept escort missions from merchants on the outskirts.
In Hekatai, it was somewhat on the outer side, but the city had likely expanded later. The Adventurer Guild was quite a bit inside when viewed from the barrier. This is common in older cities.

However, the atmosphere remained unchanged. Compared to Faltarl, the scale was many times larger, but the bustling adventurers and merchants in the early morning main street evoked a sense of nostalgia.
However, the nostalgia faded as soon as they entered the Adventurer Guild.
The moment they stepped inside, they noticed a different atmosphere. It felt like they were being watched by multiple eyes.
In fact, there were an absurd number of magical energy lines directed toward them.
It was understandable that the attention was on Erika; after all, she was beautiful. If she didn't draw attention, it would mean that everyone around her had terrible eyesight.
But why was the focus on me as well? It felt like I was being appraised.
In the Faltarl Adventurer Guild, it wouldn't matter who walked in; it never felt like this.
Even when I entered as a twelve-year-old, trying to become an adventurer while clearly showing my noble status, I received attention, but it faded quickly.
Is it just a matter of changing locations?

I intentionally ignored the gazes, and while Erika was likely aware of them, she showed no signs of concern as they made their way through the crowded guild. Their destination was the reception counter.
The guild also handled requests for escorts and specific materials, so the reception counter was where adventurers could receive or confirm requests.
In most Adventurer Guilds, this is also where registration procedures are conducted.
We stood in front of one of the reception counters that happened to be free. There was a petite woman at the counter, but for some reason, she looked clearly frightened of us.
Even if told to fight monsters without weapons, she wouldn't have such a despairing expression.
I exchanged glances with Erika.
We both had expressions that seemed to say, "You don't have any idea what this is about, do you?"
I felt like tilting my head, but I couldn't just stand silently in front of the counter, so I spoke to the guild staff.
"I'd like to register with the guild; is this the right counter?"
The response was silence.
The female guild staff and I ended up staring at each other.
I couldn't endure the ten seconds of silence.
"Y-yes!"

The response was an unexpectedly loud voice. The gazes that had scattered to sneak peeks at us concentrated back on us in droves. Did I unknowingly do something? The only thing I could think of was marrying the excessively beautiful Erika.
I began to lose confidence in my past actions due to the guild staff's unexpectedly extreme reaction.
To be honest, I felt like I was about to despair at the guild staff's attitude, but since I couldn't just leave, I asked again.
"I'd like to register as an adventurer."
This time, the guild staff's reaction was slightly better.
"Y-yes, we can accept registrations here."
She was stuttering, but was she okay?
"Then I'd like to register both myself and her as adventurers."
I wondered if they used the same adventurer registration form in the Orclra Kingdom as I waited for the guild staff's response, and I noticed that the guild staff was staring intently at my face.
This situation had happened just a moment ago.
As I was about to prompt her to speak, the female guild staff opened her mouth first.
"Um! May I ask your names!?"
Never mind asking, they’ll know when they register.
